name: Wang Haibin
current_role: Listed by Hurun (Global Unicorn Index 2026) as founder of BioRay Biopharmaceutical (Zhejiang, ~$2B); role not confirmed

BioRay focuses on autoimmune diseases and cancer, with seven marketed products, 10+ clinical-stage candidates and 1,600+ staff in Taizhou, Hangzhou, Shanghai and San Diego. No company source we could access names Wang Haibin.

notes: Identity and role unverified: BioRay's own pages (news included) do not mention him. Do not confuse with BIORAY, the US herbal-supplement brand (bioray.com). Needs a manual check (e.g. BioRay's HKEX filing or the Hisun Pharma annual report) before outreach.

name: Tim Glaser
profile: Engineer who co-founded PostHog with James Hawkins on 23 January 2020 in Y Combinator's W20 batch. PostHog grew from open-source product analytics into a full product/data platform (session replay, feature flags, experiments, data warehouse, AI) with 100,000+ customers. It has been cash-flow positive since Dec 2024 and raised a $70M Stripe-led Series D and a $75M Series E in 2025; valued $1B+.
interesting_fact: PostHog launched its MVP on Hacker News just four weeks after the founders started writing code. Later it moved from PostgreSQL to ClickHouse to support billions of events.
deep_cut_fact: PostHog was not Glaser and Hawkins's first idea. Their first startup together (Aug 2019) aimed to help engineers manage technical debt; it didn't work, but it convinced them to treat 'growth as an engineering problem.'
notes: More engineering-focused and lower profile than co-CEO James Hawkins, who handles most public comms. No personal social handle was confirmed on PostHog pages (profiles are client-rendered); use press@posthog.com or go via Hawkins.

name: Chris Best
profile: Canadian tech entrepreneur who co-founded Kik Messenger, then in 2017 co-founded Substack with fellow Kik alum Jairaj Sethi and ex-PandoDaily reporter Hamish McKenzie. Substack's subscription platform lets writers, podcasters and video creators earn directly from paying readers. In 2025 it raised $100M at a $1.1B valuation, with investors including Andreessen Horowitz.
interesting_fact: Substack raised $100M in 2025 at a $1.1B valuation (reported by The New York Times), a decade after Best co-founded the messaging app Kik.
deep_cut_fact: Best and McKenzie have cited Ben Thompson's paid newsletter Stratechery as a key inspiration for Substack. When they personally recruited a small pool of launch writers in 2017, Bill Bishop's China newsletter Sinocism was among the first to join.
notes: A podcast/media-native CEO who has given many long-form interviews, so a good podcast fit. A personal Substack/X handle could not be verified: substack.com/@chrisbest is a different person and x.com/cjgbest returned 404 to our fetch. Use press@substackinc.com or the founders' On Substack posts.
